questions.text: What is the register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: ID 0x00 RO, ENABLE 0x04 RW, PERIOD_REQ 0x08 RW, PERIOD_EFF 0x0C RO, STATUS 0x10 RO, FRAMES 0x14 RO, OVERRUNS 0x18 RO, COUNTER 0x1C RO, TAKE 0x20 WO, TICK 0x24 WO, all 32-bit word offsets
questions.reason: the request names registers but gives no offsets and the shell host needs them
questions.answer:
FRAMES: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames that fell due and were held, wrapping
STAT: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: [0] a frame waits, [1] enabled
OVERRUNS: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames dropped because one was waiting, wrapping
REQ: offset 0x01, RW, reset 100: [15:0] period asked for, as written
TICK: offset 0x03, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks, one per clock; reads 0
CTRL: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [0] enable
CNT: offset 0x08, RO, reset 0: [15:0] ticks counted towards the next frame
TAKE: offset 0x04, WO, reset 0: any write takes the waiting frame; reads 0
EFF: offset 0x02, RO, reset 100: [15:0] period in force
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: unlisted offsets: read 0, writes dropped; read-only registers also drop writes
questions.evidence: FRAMES: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames that fell due and were held, wrapping

questions.text: Does the period in force read the latched value or the live max(PERIOD_REQ, PERIOD_MIN)?
questions.default: the latched value used by the current count, updated at wrap or enable
questions.reason: the request says a new request takes effect from the start of the next count
questions.answer: The period in force (EFF) reads the latched value. It is not live max(REQ, PERIOD_MIN). EFF is loaded from the request raised to PERIOD_MIN when the count wraps, and at switch-on. A new request applies from the next count or the switch-on.
questions.evidence: Enabled: each tick adds 1 to CNT; when CNT reaches EFF it returns to 0, EFF takes the request raised to PERIOD_MIN, and a frame falls due.

questions.text: What does COUNTER read, and does it reach the period or period-1?
questions.default: COUNTER counts 0 to period-1 and wraps to 0 on the period-th tick, which is when the frame falls due
questions.reason: this gives a frame on every 100th tick exactly
questions.answer: The spec has no register named COUNTER; the counting register is CNT (offset 0x08, RO, reset 0, '[15:0] ticks counted towards the next frame'). Per the pacer behaviour, CNT counts up toward EFF and reaches the period itself (not period-1): on the tick where CNT reaches EFF it returns to 0 and a frame falls due. The proposed default's 'counts 0 to period-1' is not supported by the spec.
questions.evidence: Enabled: each tick adds 1 to CNT; when CNT reaches EFF it returns to 0, EFF takes the request raised to PERIOD_MIN, and a frame falls due.

questions.text: If a TAKE write and a due frame fall in the same clock, which wins?
questions.default: the take is applied first so the new frame is held
questions.reason: the request does not say and this loses no frame
questions.answer: the take is applied first so the new frame is held

questions.text: Does a request write while disabled update the period in force immediately?
questions.default: no, it is loaded at the next enable
questions.reason: the request says a new request takes effect from the moment reporting is switched on
questions.answer: No. A request write while disabled does not change the period in force (EFF). The new request is loaded into EFF at the next switch-on (enable going 0 to 1), so the proposed default is consistent with the spec.
questions.evidence: Switch-on (0 to 1) clears CNT and loads EFF from the request

questions.reason: the request says switching on starts from zero and leaves only the totals as they are
questions.answer: Yes, with a naming correction. The spec has no COUNTER register; the count is CNT (offset 0x08). Switch-off clears CNT. The spec does not say separately that CNT keeps reading 0 for as long as the pacer stays disabled, so the 'reads 0 while disabled' part is not specified.
questions.evidence: Switch-on (0 to 1) clears CNT and loads EFF from the request; switch-off clears CNT and the waiting frame; totals persist until reset; writing 1 while on does nothing.

questions.text: What are the values of CLKS_PER_BIT, TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: the request names them but gives no values
questions.answer: CLKS_PER_BIT is 868. TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not 1000000 as proposed. BUILD_STAMP is not specified.

questions.text: What happens on a TICK write while a burst is still in progress?
questions.default: it is ignored, since the request guarantees it does not happen
questions.answer: it is ignored, since the request guarantees it does not happen
